A.explanation: A larger grating to screen distance magnifies the pattern, so for the same diffraction angle $\theta$ the distance $x$ on the screen increases.

B.explanation: Smaller slit separation $d$ gives larger $\sin\theta = n\lambda/d$, so the angles and the separation on the screen increase.

C.explanation: Fewer slits per unit length means larger slit separation $d$, so $\sin\theta = n\lambda/d$ is smaller and the maxima move closer together.

D.explanation: Red light has longer wavelength $\lambda$ than green light, so $\sin\theta = n\lambda/d$ is larger and the separation increases.

hints: Notice the positions are set by the grating equation $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ for green light of fixed $\lambda$.
Connect angle to screen position: for a distant screen at distance $D$, the $n$th maximum is at about $x = D\tan\theta$, so smaller $\theta$ means smaller separation.
Ask what fewer slits per unit length does to the slit separation $d$, and then what larger $d$ does to $\sin\theta$ when $\lambda$ is unchanged.
walkthrough: Recall the governing rule for normal incidence: $d\sin\theta_n = n\lambda$, where $d$ is separation between adjacent slits, $\lambda$ is wavelength of the green light, and $\theta_n$ is the angle of the $n$th order maximum.
Link angle to the screen: with grating to screen distance $D$, the linear position is $x_n = D\tan\theta_n$, so decreasing $\theta_n$ decreases the spacing between maxima.
For fixed $\lambda$, $\sin\theta_n$ is proportional to $1/d$. Increasing $d$ therefore reduces $\theta_n$ and reduces $x_n$.
Fewer slits per unit length $N$ means $d = 1/N$ is larger. Hence the diffraction angles shrink and the maxima become closer together. This is option C.
